description: Figure 16c illustrates the relationship between confidence and accuracy for the MMLU Pro dataset. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.00 to 1.00, with tick labels at intervals of 0.05. The y-axis is labeled “accuracy” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. There are three lines displayed: a green dashed line with triangle markers representing “Initial Accuracy”, a blue solid line with circle markers representing “Accuracy”, and a red dashed line with square markers representing “Final Accuracy”. The “Initial Accuracy” line starts at approximately 0.18 at an initial confidence of 0.00 and ends at approximately 0.82 at an initial confidence of 1.00, showing a generally increasing trend. The “Accuracy” line begins at approximately 0.16 at an initial confidence of 0.00 and rises to approximately 0.88 at an initial confidence of 1.00, also demonstrating a generally increasing trend. Finally, the “Final Accuracy” line starts at approximately 0.25 at an initial confidence of 0.00 and increases to approximately 0.96 at an initial confidence of 1.00, exhibiting a similar increasing trend.
